# Robust Breusch–Pagan test with bootstrap and effect sizes

<small>Source: [`R/robust_implementations.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/robust_implementations.R) · Help: `?performBPTestRobust`</small>

Enhances [`performBPTest()`](performBPTest.md) by optionally studentising residuals, resampling the
test statistic via bootstrap, and reporting effect sizes together with power
diagnostics.

## Usage

```r
performBPTestRobust(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  studentize = TRUE,
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  B = 999,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  parallel = FALSE,
  studentized
)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object describing the mean structure whose
    residual variance is to be assessed.

`data`
:   A [base::data.frame](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html) (or compatible object) containing the
    variables referenced in `model`. The data must include all observations used
    to fit `model` and should not contain unresolved missing values.
    When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. It holds the
    terms of the model rather than its variables (`log(x)` rather than `x`), so
    a model that transforms a variable needs `data`, as does a
    model with an `offset()` term, and so may a fit whose `weights` or `offset`
    argument is a column of the data, which the model frame holds as
    `(weights)` or `(offset)`.

`studentize`
:   Logical, use studentized residuals for the auxiliary
    regression (Koenker variant)? Defaults to `TRUE`. The name matches
    `lmtest::bptest()` and [`performHarveyTest()`](performHarveyTest.md).

`bootstrap`
:   Logical, compute bootstrap diagnostics for the
    statistic and p-value? The bootstrap is [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md), so on
    a fit returned by [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md) each replicate estimates the weights again,
    its default since 0.15.0. There is no argument to hold them fixed here;
    [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md) with `reestimate_weights = FALSE` does that.

`B`
:   Number of bootstrap replications when `bootstrap = TRUE`.
    Defaults to 999, at which a bootstrap p-value of the form
    `(1 + #) / (B + 1)` gives an exact test at the 5% and 1% levels; it was
    1000 before 0.15.0. The value is recorded in `robust_details$bootstrap$B`
    whether or not the bootstrap runs.

`ci_level`
:   Confidence level for reported intervals.

`parallel`
:   Logical, allow parallel bootstrap evaluation when the
    `parallel` package is available. A seeded call gives the same result
    each time; see *Parallel replicates* in [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md).

`studentized`
:   Deprecated since 0.15.0: use `studentize`. It is still
    accepted, with a warning, and does what `studentize` does; it stops
    working in 1.0.0.

## Value

An augmented `htest` object containing a
`robust_details` element describing the additional diagnostics. Its
`studentized` field records the value of `studentize`.

## Details

Offers expanded reporting for the Breusch–Pagan family of tests including
bootstrap p-values and asymptotic confidence intervals. The optional
`studentize` argument toggles between the classic and Koenker versions.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. With `studentize = TRUE`, the default, it refuses a model
with an offset, which the studentized statistic leaves out when it refits the design, until the
offset fix planned for 0.16.0 (decided 2026-10-17); with `studentize = FALSE` it accounts for
it. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in [`test_results`](test_results.md), under
*Supported models*.

## References

Breusch, T. S., & Pagan, A. R. (1979). A simple test for heteroscedasticity
and random coefficient variation. *Econometrica, 47*(5), 1287–1294.

Koenker, R. (1981). A note on studentizing a test for heteroscedasticity.
*Journal of Econometrics, 17*(1), 107–112.

## See also

[`performBPTest()`](performBPTest.md) for the baseline test and [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md) for the
standalone studentised variant.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
mod <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
performBPTestRobust(mod, mtcars, bootstrap = TRUE, B = 200)
```
